newsitem.title: ITALY: MOTOR RACING-HILL IN LIMBO AS SCHUMACHER WINS OVER FANS.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-HILL IN LIMBO AS SCHUMACHER WINS OVER FANS.

text.p: Briton Damon Hill flew out of Italy to a training camp in Austria with his future still in limbo after watching his old rival Michael Schumacher earn himself a true place in the hearts of Ferrari fans.

Hill, who kept his 13-point championship lead intact despite spinning out when he hit a stack of tyres, had been favourite to win the Italian Grand Prix, but ended up surveying Schumacher's triumph -- and emotional reception from the fans -- on television.
The German's win, the 22nd of his career and his third in his first season for Ferrari, was his first for the team on Italian soil and their first at Monza since 1988.

Schumacher can now expect to be heralded as a true hero for the Maranello-based team -- who greeted him as `the ice man' after his signing from Benetton last year -- and may also usher in a new era for Ferrari.
Team chief Jean Todt, who had been given a target of two victories by Ferrari president Luca di Montezemolo at the start of the season, was overwhelmed, but determined to maintain their progress.

Todt said: "It is fantastic to win here at Monza in front of so many people who were urging us on and who deserved to be repaid for all their passion. I am particularly happy because I know how much hard work and dedication from everyone at Ferrari went into this success.

"Michael was exceptional, but the team also helped him perfectly. I am sorry for Eddie (Irvine), who could have finished on the podium, but I am sure he will see happier days. Now we will enjoy our triumph for a few hours and then, on Monday morning at eight, we will start work again to improve still further."

For the other teams, Todt's determination will ring as a warning that Ferrari now appear to have regained reliability and emerged as serious challengers for the constructors' championship next season.
Schumacher won with a virtuouso performance while Irvine was, like Hill and five others, a victim of the tyres piled up to protect the cars from hitting loose concrete kerbs at the chicanes.

The double world champion now looks likely to play a decisive part in the final two races, but may not be able to prevent Hill from taking the title. With two races remaining in Estoril and Suzuka, his 13 points lead should be enough to seal the title.

Canadian Jacques Villeneuve, his Williams team-mate, is his only rival, but requires a victory and at least a podium finish -- with Hill failing to score a point -- if he is to claim the title. Villeneuve, however, refused to give up after the race and said that while it remained mathematically possible for him to win the title, he would fight on.

Schumacher said: "I have to say I was lucky today, because without Damon going into the tyre barrier it would have been a lot more difficult. But, even so, looking at the lap times, we were competitive in the race and I think we would have been able to fight with the Williams.
"Whether we would have been able to take them or not is a different question. It is going to be a lot more difficult on the circuits we are going to next.

"At Estoril, the surface is slippery and the tyres will be used so hard it is going to be difficult to keep them together, especially on our car. To be honest, I dont think Estoril will be very kind to us.
"Suzuka is a circuit I like very much so I am hoping the car will suit the circuit there and we can get another win."
